## Security verdict: PASS

PR #223 at **881a3f568e6c078d5f642c3574ddc9813902838f**, under C33/C34. Reviewed the seven-file delta and directly relevant read-scope, reply-evidence and presentation paths.

The local ID lookup does not grant new cross-project visibility: existing recognized local callers can explicitly select another existing project for request listing, without a project-membership gate (`crates/daemon/src/http/requests.rs:65-90,216-254`; `http/directory.rs:1868-1912`; `crates/store/src/role_requests.rs:1153-1196`). The warning discloses only metadata within that existing local read surface.

**Federation is separately guarded, not assumed trusted by C33.** Peer authentication stamps `from_machine` and provides no reply evidence (`http/mod.rs:1975-2044`). Ordinary forwarded sends skip the answer/warning call (`2110-2164`). Peer FYIs may reach the helper, but missing evidence returns before the new warning lookup (`2336-2378,2509-2520`). Thus neither path exposes these new request existence/holder/state warnings to a remote peer.

Warning reasons use fixed text, `render::msg_id`, `render::seat` and enum state spelling (`http/mod.rs:2381-2417`). Closed warnings contain no close reason or request body. Ordinary message correlation adds no warning.

Answering authority remains separate: existing pane/native-session sender binding, delivered-state and recorded-holder checks remain; the store preserves the first answer and its transactional audit (`http/mod.rs:2236-2378`; `delivery/role_send.rs:1193-1235`; `store/src/role_requests.rs:799-830`). The new warning helper reads only; it does not close or stamp requests. Refused receipts do not trigger answering.

|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | None identified in scoped changes | - |

Known limits remain: no auto-close, role-addressed replies discard the optional note, and an unknown ID cannot be distinguished from an ordinary message. Added assertions cover holder/repeat/ordinary correlation and answered labels, not every cross-project, FYI/shim or reason branch end to end; no exhaustive runtime claim is made.
